posts.name: three-lies

slides.label: LIE #1
slides.emphasis: Then why do you feel worse after?

slides.label: LIE #3
slides.sub: The screen never shows who chose to be there. Real people aren't scripts.

posts.caption:
3 lies p*rn tells you, and why they keep you stuck.

1. "It helps me relax." The relief lasts minutes. The fog and regret last the rest of the night.
2. "I can stop anytime." If that were true, you'd have stopped already. Today is a good day to prove it.
3. "It's harmless." P*rn is staged and scripted, and the screen never shows whether the person in it actually chose to be there.

Which lie kept you stuck the longest? Tell us below. 👇

Save this for a hard night.

posts.name: friction

reel.closing: Guardian puts a wall between you and p*rn.

posts.caption:
You won't out-willpower a p*rn site at midnight. Design beats willpower.

P*rn needs speed. So make it slow: phone charges outside the bedroom, browsers logged out, a blocker switched on. When it takes ten steps instead of one, the urge usually passes before you get there.

Guardian builds that pause in for you: a curtain over p*rn sites, so you get a moment to choose. 🛠️

posts.name: what-it-costs
posts.caption:
P*rn doesn't just cost you 20 minutes. It costs you the next morning: the fog, the shame, the half-there conversations.

Quit, and the people in your life get the version of you that's present. Rested. Not carrying a secret.

That's what you're fighting for. Tag someone who's quitting with you. 💜

posts.name: how-long

reel.closing: Day 20 feels hard? That's normal. Keep going.

posts.caption:
When does quitting p*rn get easier?

There's no exact number for p*rn. But in one study on building new daily habits, it took anywhere from 18 to 254 days for a habit to feel automatic, typically around 66. And missing a single day didn't derail it.

So if day 20 still feels hard, you're not failing. You're in the middle. 🌿

What day are you on? Drop it below.

(Source: Lally et al., European Journal of Social Psychology, 2010)

posts.name: not-the-only-one

lines.lead: Think you're the only one hooked on p*rn?

posts.caption:
It can feel like you're the only one who can't stop watching p*rn. You're not. Not even close.

All over the world, people are quitting and pushing back against an industry built to keep you clicking. Every day you stay off it, you're part of that.

If you're in this fight, comment ✊. Let the next guy see he's not alone.

posts.name: thirty-days
posts.caption:
30 days p*rn-free. A whole month of choosing yourself.

If you're there, stop and take it in. Nobody saw most of those wins: a phone put down, a walk taken, a night you went to bed instead.

What changed most for you since quitting? Tell us below. Someone on day 3 needs to read it. 💛

posts.name: how-far

reel.closing: Keep going. One day at a time.

posts.caption:
Whatever this month of quitting p*rn looked like, perfect or messy, you know more than you did on day one.

You know your danger hours. You know an urge peaks and passes. You know your why.

That doesn't go away. Keep going. 🧡
